dimensions.assessment: Directly affects college student athletes, prospective student athletes, Division I institutions, athletic conferences, intercollegiate athletic associations, athlete agents, and HBCUs nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: student athletes and prospective student athletes and the parents or guardians of student athletes or prospective student athletes

dimensions.assessment: Substantial changes to the legal and financial conditions of student athletes, including mandated NIL rights, agent fee caps, mandatory medical and post-eligibility coverage, and strict transfer rules.
dimensions.evidence: an Act To protect the name, image, and likeness rights of, and provide protections for, student athletes and to promote fair competition among intercollegiate athletics

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes appropriations of $180,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2032 for the HBCU Sports Media and Connectivity Program, establishes a $60,000,000 minimum annual fund for post-eligibility medical expenses, and involves multi-million dollar retention funds.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this title $180,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2032.

dimensions.assessment: Creates multiple new federal programs, extensive statutory requirements for athletic associations, amendments to the Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961 and the Sports Agent Responsibility and Trust Act, and preempts conflicting state laws.
dimensions.evidence: No State or political subdivision of a State may adopt, maintain, enforce, or continue in effect any law, regulation, rule, requirement, or standard that conflicts with any provision of this title

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory provisions combined with multi-year grant authorizations running through fiscal year 2032 and specific provisions with 4-year or 9-year sunsets.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this title $180,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2032.

importance_detail.rationale: S. 4668 enacts sweeping nationwide changes across college athletics by establishing statutory protections and rules for name, image, and likeness (NIL) agreements, athlete agent regulations, medical coverage requirements, antitrust exemptions for media rights pooling under the Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961, and authorization of $180,000,000 annually for an HBCU sports media and connectivity program.

other.label: CBO cost estimate: S. 4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026

summary: The Protect College Sports Act of 2026 establishes federal rules governing name, image, and likeness (NIL) agreements for college student athletes, creates limited antitrust exemptions for sports broadcasting rights, and sets standards for student health, safety, transfers, and scholarship protections. It also establishes a competitive grant program to improve broadband, technology, and sports media infrastructure at Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs).

affected_groups.effect: Allowed to enter NIL agreements and transfer once without losing athletic eligibility, while gaining enhanced medical coverage, scholarship protections, and ombudsman support.
Subject to new disclosure requirements, revenue share caps, mandatory student health standards, and restrictions on cutting non-revenue or Olympic sports programs.
Required to register with states and athletic associations, with endorsement fees capped at 5 percent.
Eligible to apply for competitive federal grants to improve campus broadband, information technology, and sports media infrastructure.

key_provisions: Prohibits institutions and athletic associations from restricting student athletes' NIL agreements or revoking grants-in-aid based on NIL earnings, while requiring students to report NIL compensation exceeding $600.
Provides an antitrust exemption for schools and conferences forming joint agreements to pool and sell college sports media rights, subject to certain conditions and revenue-sharing formulas.
Grants student athletes the ability to transfer once between four-year institutions without losing athletic eligibility.
Establishes strict health, wellness, and safety standards, requiring independent medical personnel authority and designated institutional health and safety officers.
Creates a Congressional Commission on the Future of College Athletics to study long-term compensation, student protection, and sports governance structures.
Authorizes $180,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2032 for the HBCU Sports Media and Connectivity Program to fund broadband and sports broadcast infrastructure.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact level of future appropriations beyond the authorized totals for the HBCU program.
Exact outcomes of the court-approved 'In Re College Athlete NIL Litigation' settlement referenced throughout the bill text.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Protect College Sports Act of 2026 establishes federal rules governing name, image, and likeness (NIL) agreements for college student athletes, creates limited antitrust exemptions for sports broadcasting rights, and sets standards for student health, safety, transfers, and scholarship protections. It also establishes a competitive grant program to improve broadband, technology, and sports media infrastructure at Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs).
summary_detail.significance: The bill comprehensively alters the regulatory landscape of collegiate athletics by codifying NIL rights, creating uniform national standards for transfers and medical care, and adjusting antitrust laws for broadcast pooling. It impacts nearly all Division I athletic programs, major athletic conferences, and student athletes across the United States.

title: Protect College Sports Act of 2026
